component.name: GameHandler
component.summary: Run Windows games on Linux with Wine and Proton

description.p: GameHandler is a modern game manager for Linux, focused on running Windows games through Wine and Proton. It provides a native interface built with libcosmic, the COSMIC desktop toolkit, for organising your library, downloading Proton and Wine builds, and launching games in isolated prefixes.

GameHandler is a front-end, not a compatibility layer. Windows games run on Wine, usually through a Proton build maintained by someone else, with Direct3D translated by DXVK and VKD3D-Proton. GameHandler downloads those builds from their maintainers own release pages, sets up isolated prefixes, and stays out of their way. A Credits page inside the application names every upstream project it depends on.
Features:

ul.li: Light and dark modes, plus following the system theme
Categorize games and filter the library
Custom covers, Steam artwork lookup, or the executable's own icon
Add Windows or Linux games and pick a runner per title
Download Proton-GE, Proton-CachyOS, Proton-EM, and Kron4ek Wine builds
Guide for which Proton or Wine family to use
Detect optional MangoHud, GameMode, Winetricks, and UMU helpers
Lutris-style Esync and Fsync toggles per game
Easy installers for store launchers and common Windows apps
Credits page listing every upstream project, with links and licenses

description.p: The interface has been rewritten on libcosmic, the COSMIC desktop toolkit, in Rust. Nothing of the Python and Qt 6/Kirigami stack remains in the shipped application: the library, the runner downloads, the launch environment and the cover handling are a Rust workspace now, and the Flatpak is built from a Cargo lockfile on the Freedesktop runtime instead of a Meson build on the KDE runtime.

Nothing about your data changes. The library and settings files are read and written in the same format as before — byte for byte, including numeric timestamps — so an existing installation keeps its games, covers, prefixes and preferences, and either version can open the same data directory.
Light and dark themes remain first-class alongside following the system theme, and the interface renders on the CPU, so it opens a window on a machine with no working GPU.
Fix headless unittest discovery without PySide6 by loading the test-only Kirigami stub lazily, with regression coverage for the optional QML smoke test skip.
Align the Flatpak with KDE and PySide 6.10, add a Gosh-identified About and Credits page, synchronize release metadata, and correct the documented test command.

The interface has been rewritten from scratch on Qt 6 and KDE's Kirigami framework; nothing of the old GTK and libadwaita stack remains. Light and dark modes are both first-class, alongside following the system theme.

Games and covers picked from network shares now work: locations such as smb:// are resolved through their mounted GVFS path instead of asking another application to open them, and a share that is not mounted says so with an instruction rather than failing silently.
Winetricks and winecfg now run with the same Wine build the game uses, so prefixes created by a downloaded Proton or Wine build are no longer refused or silently migrated by the system Wine.

A bug-fix release for adding and starting titles. Easy installers now wait for the vendor's own wizard to finish instead of scanning the prefix while it is still open, and they find what Proton installed: a Proton prefix keeps its files one directory deeper, which used to make every Proton install look like a missing executable. A finished install offers to start the launcher straight away.

Artwork lookup no longer attaches the wrong cover. A store launcher is not a Steam product, so searching Steam for one returned an unrelated game; those matches are now rejected, and Windows titles Steam has never sold fall back to the icon their executable already carries. Lookups that find nothing say so instead of failing in silence.
A game that exits the moment it starts now reports why, rather than leaving a "Launching..." message behind and no window.

A polish and hardening release. The library grid now tiles correctly instead of showing one card per row, games without artwork get a generated cover, and the library gained sorting plus a remove confirmation. Downloaded runner archives are extracted with path traversal protection, and desktop shortcuts escape their values.

Adds a Credits page acknowledging Wine, Proton, DXVK, VKD3D-Proton, the Proton and Wine build maintainers, and the launchers GameHandler learned from, together with the reasoning behind shipping one app instead of asking people to assemble the stack themselves.
Lutris-style compatibility toggles: DXVK, VKD3D, NVAPI/DLSS, FSR, BattlEye, Easy Anti-Cheat, Gamescope, a Wine virtual desktop, and free-form environment variables.
Easy Installer downloads now require an approved HTTPS origin and a valid Authenticode signature from the expected software publisher.
Per-game Esync and Fsync toggles, plus a catalog of easy installers for Battle.net, Epic, EA App, Ubisoft Connect, GOG Galaxy, Amazon Games, Rockstar, Steam, and Discord.
Categories, custom and Steam-fetched covers, a runner chooser guide, and install offers for MangoHud and other launch plugins.
Dark mode, a redesigned library, and built-in downloads for ProtonPlus-style Proton and Wine families. Games can pick a runner at install time and change it later.
Initial release with library management and Wine/Proton launching.
